text: Accurately predicting date target number subjects events achieved critical planning, monitoring, execution clinical trials. eventPred package provides enrollment event prediction capabilities using assumed enrollment treatment-specific time--event models design stage, using blinded unblinded data specified enrollment time--event models analysis stage. design stage, enrollment often specified using piecewise Poisson process constant enrollment rate specified time interval. analysis stage, enrollment completion, eventPred package considers several models, including homogeneous Poisson model, time-decay model enrollment rate function \(\lambda(t) = (\mu/\delta) (1 - \exp(-\delta t))\), B-spline model daily enrollment rate \(\lambda(t) = \exp(B(t)'\theta)\), piecewise Poisson model. prior information exists model parameters, can combined likelihood yield posterior distribution. eventPred package also offers several time--event models, including exponential, Weibull, log-logistic, log-normal, piecewise exponential, model averaging Weibull log-normal, spline, cox. time dropout, set model options considered. enrollment complete, ongoing subjects event interest dropped study data cut contribute additional events future. event times generated conditional distribution given survived data cut. new subjects need enrolled, enrollment time event time can generated specified enrollment time--event models parameters drawn posterior distribution. Time--dropout can generated similar fashion. eventPred package displays Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) fitted curve overlaid observed data help users select appropriate model enrollment event prediction. Prediction intervals prediction plot can used measure prediction uncertainty, simulated enrollment event data can used data exploration. useful function eventPred package getPrediction, combines model fitting, data simulation, summary simulation results. functions perform individual tasks can used select appropriate prediction model. eventPred package implements model parameterization enhances asymptotic normality parameter estimates. Specifically, package utilizes following parameterization achieve goal: Enrollment models Poisson: \(\theta = \log(\lambda)\). Time-decay: \(\theta = (\log(\mu), \log(\delta))'\). B-spline: \(\log(\lambda(t)) = B(t)' \theta\), \(B(t) = (B_1(t), \ldots, B_{k+4}(t))'\) B-spline basis \(k\) inner knots. Piecewise Poisson: \(\theta_j = \log(\lambda_j)\) \(j\)th time interval. left endpoints time intervals, denoted accrualTime, considered fixed. Event dropout models Let \(x\) denote covariates subject. Let \(\beta\) denote regression coefficients \(\sigma\) denote scale parameter AFT model, $$\log(T) = \beta' x + \sigma \epsilon.$$ Exponential: \(\log(\lambda) = \theta' x\). words, \(\theta = -\beta\). Weibull: \(\log(\texttt{weibull scale}) = \theta_1' x\), \(\log(\texttt{weibull shape}) = -\theta_2\). words, \(\theta = (\beta', \log(\sigma))'\). Log-logistic: logistic distribution \(\log(T)\), \(\texttt{location} = \theta_1' x\), \(\log(\texttt{scale}) = \theta_2\). words, \(\theta = (\beta', \log(\sigma))'\). Log-normal: normal distribution \(\log(T)\), \(\texttt{mean} = \theta_1' x\), \(\log(\texttt{sd}) = \theta_2\). words, \(\theta = (\beta', \log(\sigma))'\). Piecewise exponential: \(\log(\lambda_j) = \theta_{1j} + \theta_2' x\) \(j\)th time interval, \(\theta = (\theta_1', \theta_2')'\). left endpoints time intervals, denoted piecewiseSurvivalTime event model piecewiseDropoutTime dropout model, considered fixed. Model averaging: \(\theta = (\theta_{\texttt{weibull}}',     \theta_{\texttt{lnorm}}')'\). covariance matrix \(\theta\) structured block diagonal matrix, upper-left block corresponding Weibull component lower-right block corresponding log-normal component. words, covariance matrix partitioned two distinct blocks, -diagonal elements connecting two components. weight assigned Weibull component, denoted \(w_1\), considered fixed. Spline: Let \(S(t|x)\) denote survival function given covariates \(x\). model transformation survival function cubic spine: $$g(S(t|x)) = c(u) + \theta_2' x,$$ $$c(u) = \gamma_1 + \gamma_2 u + \gamma_3 v_1(u) + \cdots +     \gamma_{k+2} v_k(u)$$ cubic spline \(u=\log(t)\), \(\theta = (\theta_1', \theta_2')'\), \(\theta_1 = (\gamma_1, \ldots, \gamma_{k+2})'\), assuming \(k\) inner knots (\(k = \texttt{knots}\)), \(v_1(u), \ldots, v_k(u)\) basis Royston/Parmar spline. transformation given follows: scale = "hazard", \(g(S(t)) = \log(-\log(S(t)))\). scale = "odds",  \(g(S(t)) = \log(1/S(t)-1)\). scale = "normal", \(g(S(t)) = -\Phi^{-1}(S(t))\). hazard, odds, normal scales correspond extensions Weibull, log-logistic, log-normal distributions, respectively. Cox: Let \(t_1 < \cdots < t_M\) denote distinct observed event times, \(\lambda_j\) denote estimated baseline hazard rate \(j\)th time interval, \((t_{j-1}, t_j]\), \(\beta\) denote regression coefficients (log hazard ratios) Cox model. model parameters including baseline hazards \(\theta = (\log(\lambda_1),\ldots,\log(\lambda_M), \beta^T)^T\). eventPred package uses days primary time unit. need convert enrollment event rates per month rates per day, simply divide 30.4375.
